source_anchors.locator: Sura 108:1 interpretation list, online lines 49-51; Qurtubi's citation is the list's following named entry after item 15
source_anchors.witness: وقال ابن إسحاق : هو العظيم من الأمر ; وذكر بيت لبيد ... أي عظيم
source_anchors.finding: The Qurtubi authorial text explicitly attributes this opinion to Ibn Ishaq and says he cites a Labid line. The passage itself provides no isnad or transmitting route.

source_anchors.work: Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya, section 'نزول سورة الكوثر' / 'صاحبا ملحوب والرداع'
source_anchors.witness: قال ابن إسحاق : قال لبيد بن ربيعة الكلابي ... وصاحب ملحوب فجعنا بيومه وعند الرداع بيت آخر كوثر ... يقول : عظيم
source_anchors.finding: The parallel Sira witness explicitly frames the verse as Ibn Ishaq's citation of Labid and gives بيومه, whereas the Qurtubi tafsir witness has بفقده. Ibn Hisham then identifies the two place/person references and glosses the poem's كوثر as 'much'; this is a poetic/lexical context, not independent proof that the poem itself defines Qur'anic al-Kawthar.

source_comparison.claim_boundary: Q04N is Qurtubi's sixteenth-positioned al-Kawthar interpretation, following the anonymous fourteenth/fifteenth pair; the stated authority is Ibn Ishaq. Keep it separate from prior anonymous Q04M and from the poem's own lexical use of كوثر.
source_comparison.voice_map: Qurtubi = compiler/authorial narrator; Ibn Ishaq = named attributor of the 'great matter' interpretation in Qurtubi's sentence; Labid ibn Rabi'a = poet cited; Ibn Hisham = separate Sira witness/editor preserving the Ibn Ishaq-to-Labid attribution.
source_comparison.variant_boundary: The two inspected witnesses differ in the first hemistich: Qurtubi stored Arabic says فجعنا بفقده, Ibn Hisham's page 394 witness says فجعنا بيومه. Preserve the row's reading; do not normalize it to the parallel.
source_comparison.gloss_boundary: Qurtubi follows the couplet with أي عظيم. Ibn Hisham has يقول عظيم and separately says the poem's كوثر means الكثير. Do not merge these glosses or claim Ibn Ishaq's direct wording beyond what each witness states.
source_comparison.route_boundary: No oral route or isnad is supplied in Qurtubi's short clause; the Sira witness states the Ibn Ishaq-to-Labid attribution but does not supply a chain to Qurtubi.
source_comparison.english_boundary: The stored English witness omits this named opinion and poem. Record the coverage gap; no new translation is proposed or written into live data.
source_comparison.attribution_limit: The Ibn Hisham parallel confirms a source-local literary attribution/variant, not the reliability of the exegesis and not an authorized replacement of Qurtubi's Arabic.
